drivers.title: Alphabet rout hits tech and AI names
drivers.text: Alphabet fell 12.6% after weaker sales growth and AI spending worries, its worst day since it began trading. The Nasdaq lost 1.4% while the S&P 500 slipped only 0.3%, as more stocks rose than fell.

drivers.title: Yields ease, but a Dec hike is priced
drivers.text: The 10-year fell 7 bp to 4.98% a day after the Fed held with two dissents for a hike. Futures show about a 71% chance of a hike on 9 Dec, as of Friday morning.

drivers.title: Oil dips on Iran diplomacy hopes
drivers.text: WTI settled at $102.00, down 0.8%, as signs of renewed talks eased fears that US strikes on Iran could restart. Oil is still above $100, which keeps energy cash flows strong.

sowhat.text: Lower yields and tighter credit spreads keep financing open, and strategic buyers are still writing large checks, as GE Vernova and DoorDash show. Grid equipment and power stay the hot industrial theme, while an AI-spending scare is a risk for tech valuations.

pitch: Stocks slipped Thursday, with the S&P 500 down about 0.3% to 7,720, but the Nasdaq fell 1.4% because Alphabet dropped 12.6% on AI spending worries. The 10-year yield eased 7 basis points to about 4.98%, even though the Fed held a day earlier and futures still lean toward a hike on December 9. Oil dipped to about 102 dollars on hopes for Iran talks. On the deal side, GE Vernova agreed to buy Trench Group from Triton for about 9 billion dollars, a grid equipment deal, and DoorDash is buying Instacart for roughly 17 billion. Credit spreads are tight, so financing is open for buyers.

quiz.q: Where did the 10-year Treasury yield end on Thursday 29 Oct, per the Treasury par yield curve?
Why did the Nasdaq fall about 1.4% while the S&P 500 fell only 0.3%?
quiz.a: Alphabet fell 12.6% on weaker sales growth and AI spending worries, hitting tech, while most S&P stocks rose.

quiz.q: Who is GE Vernova buying Trench Group from, and for how much?
quiz.a: Triton Partners, for $9B (13x 2028 adjusted EBITDA). Goldman Sachs and UBS advised GE Vernova; Bank of America and Morgan Stanley advised Triton.

chat.q: What's your read on markets this week?
chat.a: The S&P 500 closed at 7,720, down 0.3%, but the Nasdaq fell 1.4% after Alphabet dropped 12.6% on AI spending worries. The 10-year eased to 4.98%. For bankers, the question is whether the tech wobble slows financing or just resets valuations.
chat.tip: Lead with the S&P and the Alphabet reason, then pivot to deals.

chat.a: WTI settled at $102.00, down 0.8%, on hopes of Iran talks. It is still above $100, so producers and oilfield services have strong cash flow, which supports energy M&A and capex. A deal would pull prices down, and strikes would push them up.
chat.tip: Name the Iran swing factor in both directions.

chat.a: GE Vernova agreed to buy Trench Group from Triton for $9B, about 13x 2028 adjusted EBITDA, a grid equipment deal. Goldman Sachs and UBS advised the buyer; Bank of America and Morgan Stanley advised the seller. DoorDash is also buying Instacart for about $17B.
chat.tip: Name the advisers; bankers will ask who advised.

chat.q: What are you watching next week?
chat.a: Palantir reports Monday after the close, as a read on AI demand after the Alphabet drop. Friday 6 Nov is the October jobs report, which feeds the odds of a Fed hike on 9 Dec, about 71% on Friday morning.
chat.tip: Tie each event to the Fed or AI theme.

chat.q: If the 10-year rose 50 bp, what happens to a DCF?
chat.a: The 10-year is 4.98% now. A 50 bp rise lifts the risk-free rate and so the WACC, which lowers the present value of cash flows. Long-duration companies with value far out in the terminal value fall the most, and the terminal value is the most sensitive piece.
chat.tip: Say the direction, then which companies are hit hardest.

chat.q: Why might a sponsor-backed seller like Triton sell Trench now?
chat.a: Credit is open: high yield spreads were about 314 bp on 28 Oct, and strategics are active. Trench sold at 13x 2028 adjusted EBITDA to GE Vernova, a buyer with a clear grid-equipment strategy. A strategic sale to a buyer paying for growth often beats an IPO for a sponsor.
chat.tip: Mention the dual-track of sale versus IPO.

chat.q: How do the Fed and the 10-year affect M&A financing right now?
chat.a: The Fed held at 3.75–4.00% but futures price about a 71% chance of a hike on 9 Dec. The 10-year is near 4.98%, so debt is costly, yet spreads of 314 bp for high yield and 86 bp for investment grade show buyers can still borrow. DoorDash lined up a JPMorgan bridge loan for Instacart.
chat.tip: Separate the base rate from the credit spread.
